rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) - annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For covered older rental units, rent may be raised only once every 12 months, by the allowable percentage set by the city (3% for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026). Since Feb. 2, 2026 no extra percentage for utilities or for an added dependent is allowed; a 10% increase for an additional non-dependent tenant is still permitted.
rules.key_value: Once per 12 months, by annual allowable percentage (3% for 7/1/2025-6/30/2026)
rules.citation: L.A. Mun. Code ch. XV, § 151.00 et seq.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.effective_date_note: Date of the current formula changes (no utility add-on, no dependent add-on) per LAHD; the underlying RSO is much older and its original date is not in the documents.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28; apartments, duplexes, ADUs, hotel rooms held over 30 days, mobile homes in parks.
rules.exemptions: Condominiums/townhomes: rent not regulated for tenancies commencing after Dec. 31, 1995. Luxury exemption by application.
rules.interaction: Local RSO governs instead of the state cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12) where both would apply.
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates for the new formula: 2026-02-02 per LAHD (used) and 2026-01-24 per a landlord association. Local RSO governs over state Tenant Protection Act where it applies.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO - just cause, eviction notices and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO units may evict only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require a Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD first and relocation assistance paid within 15 days of notice ($11,000 to $27,400 per unit for 7/1/2026-6/30/2027). Notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days and the Notice of Right to Counsel attached.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation $11,000-$27,400 per unit (2026-27) for no-fault
rules.quoted_span: No-fault evictions require the payment of relocation assistance
rules.effective_date_note: Original effective date not stated; Right to Counsel notice required from 2025-08-20; current relocation amounts effective 2026-07-01 and increase each July 1.
rules.exemptions: No relocation when replacing a resident manager with another or for natural-disaster hazards; reduced amounts for Mom and Pop owner/family occupancy evictions; rent offset allowed.
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO; non-payment of relocation is an affirmative defense for tenants.
rules.interaction: Same relocation rules apply to JCO units (L.A. Mun. Code § 165.00 et seq.); demolition for new construction of Protected Units follows the RPO.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: For covered LA units not regulated by the RSO, a landlord may end a tenancy only for listed at-fault or no-fault reasons. No-fault evictions require relocation assistance (one month's rent for qualifying natural-person single-family dwellings). Eviction notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days, and evictions for unpaid rent are barred unless the amount owed exceeds Fair Market Rent.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.effective_date_note: Core JCO effective date not stated. Non-payment FMR threshold effective 2023-03-27; Notice of Right to Counsel from 2025-08-20.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in LA not regulated by the RSO, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and single-family dwellings; tenant must have lived 6 months or original lease expired.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless/treatment facilities, some HACLA/government properties.
rules.interaction: Applies to units not covered by the RSO; JCO does not regulate rent increases (state Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 may apply).
rules.conflict_note: LAHD page does not itself cite the code section; LAMC 165.xx citations come from LAHD relocation bulletin (D043).

rules.title: Los Angeles Resident Protections Ordinance: demolition for new construction
rules.requirement: When Protected Units are demolished for new construction, owners must pay the higher of State Housing Crisis Act or City relocation. Lower-income households get standardized payments of $87,450 to $115,480 under Option 1, plus right to remain up to 6 months, right to return and right of first refusal.
rules.key_value: $87,450 (low), $96,750 (very low), $115,480 (extremely low) per unit under Option 1
rules.quoted_span: Owners have 3 relocation options to comply with the RPO relocation rules.
rules.effective_date_note: Bulletin says RPO effective 2/11/2025; Council adopted it that day.
rules.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.interaction: Applies only to Protected Units demolished for new construction; other units follow regular RSO/JCO relocation rules.

requires_unknown_facts: unit is a Protected Unit being demolished for new construction

rules.title: LA RSO security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords of rent-stabilized units in the City of Los Angeles must pay tenants accrued interest on security deposits, monthly or yearly, as direct payment or rent credit, and tell the tenant in writing which method is used.
rules.key_value: Interest paid monthly or annually; rate set annually by the City (4.32% for 2025)
rules.quoted_span: Security deposit interest must be paid to the tenant either monthly or annually.
rules.effective_date_note: Interest began accruing November 1, 1990, per quoted code text.
rules.coverage_conditions: Properties subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.penalty: Non-compliance can be raised as a defense in eviction proceedings (per the source article).
rules.conflict_note: Source is a landlord-association article quoting the code; coverage tied to RSO status.

unverifiable_exemptions: RSO exemptions such as single-family homes and condos

no_rule_findings.finding: Only a September 2024 council motion instructing LAHD to report on algorithm-based rent-setting software and the feasibility of a ban. It is not an enacted ordinance, so the documents show no rule at the city level.
